title: Personal Checking: Deposit Availability, Mobile Deposit Acceptance and Daily Debit Limits
content:
## Posting equals availability

A deposit to a Personal Checking account is booked to the ledger on the business day its money becomes usable, so the ledger balance and the available balance are one and the same.

| Kind of credit | Business day it posts |
|---|---|
| Cash, direct deposit, other ACH credit, incoming wire, Zelle receipt, internal transfer in | the day it is received |
| Deposited check, account open at least the new-account period | the next business day |
| Deposited check, account open fewer calendar days than the new-account period | the tier's new-account hold day after the deposit |

A restricted or dormant account still takes deposits; a closed or charged-off account takes none.

## Mobile deposit acceptance

A mobile deposit is taken only if, once added, the day's mobile deposits stay within the tier's daily mobile figure and mobile deposits over the rolling 30 calendar days ending on the deposit date (that day included) stay within the tier's 30-day mobile figure. A mobile deposit over either figure is refused and never posts.

## Debit authorization limits

Debits are authorized only inside the tier's daily figures, each counted per calendar day on Eastern Time:

- ATM cash withdrawals, against the ATM figure;
- debit card purchases, against the purchase figure;
- Zelle payments, against the daily Zelle figure and also against the Zelle figure for the rolling 30 calendar days ending on the payment date, that day included.

Anything that would breach one of these figures is refused at authorization, so it never reaches the ledger. Paper checks are paid only on a tier that allows check writing. Requests for a temporary increase in any limit are not handled under this rule.

## Hypothetical checks

- A tier's daily mobile figure is 2000.00 USD; the owner deposited 1500.00 USD by mobile this morning and now tries 600.00 USD. The total would reach 2100.00 USD, so the second deposit is refused.
- A check deposited on a Monday to an account opened ten days earlier, with a hypothetical hold of three business days and no holiday that week, posts on Thursday.
